name: Nikos Christodoulides
role: President of the Republic of Cyprus (Πρόεδρος της Κυπριακής Δημοκρατίας); under Cyprus's presidential system the President is both head of state and head of government and leads the Council of Ministers
party: Independent (no party); struck off the register of the Democratic Rally (Δημοκρατικός Συναγερμός, DISY) in January 2023 for standing against its candidate — attends the leaders' summits of the European People's Party (EPP)
bio: Nikos Christodoulides (Νίκος Χριστοδουλίδης), born in Geroskipou in the Paphos district in 1973, has been President of the Republic of Cyprus since 28 February 2023; under the Cypriot presidential system he is both head of state and head of government. A career diplomat from 1999 with a doctorate in political science from the University of Athens, he was director of President Nicos Anastasiades' diplomatic office (2013–2018), government spokesman (2014–2018) and foreign minister (March 2018 – January 2022), then ran for president as an independent: the Democratic Rally (DISY) struck him off its register, and, backed by DIKO, EDEK and DIPA, he won the February 2023 run-off with 51.97% against the AKEL-backed Andreas Mavroyiannis. His term has been marked by a restrictive migration policy (a new deputy ministry, the April 2024 suspension of Syrian asylum claims and a sharp fall in arrivals, with Human Rights Watch alleging pushbacks to Lebanon, which Cypriot officials deny), the Amalthea sea corridor for aid to Gaza, a tax reform in force since January 2026 and the Cyprus presidency of the Council of the EU from January to June 2026. On the Cyprus problem he seeks the resumption of UN-led negotiations from where they stopped at Crans-Montana in 2017, on the basis of a bizonal, bicommunal federation; after informal enlarged meetings in 2025 and a visit by UN Secretary-General António Guterres in July 2026, formal negotiations had not resumed as of October 2026, with Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman asking for prior acceptance of a rotating presidency and Turkey's President Erdoğan advocating two states. Since January 2026 a covertly filmed video alleging campaign-finance breaches by people close to him ('Videogate'), later claimed by the Israeli firm Black Cube, has led to the resignation of his chief of staff and a criminal investigation still being assessed by the Attorney-General in October 2026; he did not appear in the recordings. In the May 2026 parliamentary election, which does not affect his five-year term (due to end in 2028), two of the parties supporting him, EDEK and DIPA, lost all their seats.
